answers.answer: There is a 5-day grace period. With a due date D, nothing is charged up to and including D+5; the first fee is due on D+6.
Each fee is 2% of the unpaid invoice amount (the invoice amount minus what has been paid towards it, never counting earlier fees), rounded down to the whole cent, but never less than 250 cents.

One fee per 30-day period of lateness: period 1 is due on D+6, period 2 on D+36, period 3 on D+66, and so on, while the invoice is still open. Fees do not compound: each is computed on the unpaid invoice amount alone. If assessment did not run for a while, the next run charges every period that is due and not yet charged, each computed on the unpaid amount at that moment, with `period` numbering them.
A payment covers assessed fees that are still unpaid first, and only what is left goes to the invoice amount. A payment made before a fee existed is not reallocated afterwards.

Total late fees on one invoice never exceed 25% of the invoice amount (rounded down to the cent). A fee that would cross the cap is cut down to fit, and once the cap is reached nothing more is charged (no zero-amount fees).
